title: Ris a l'amande
subtitle: Danish Christmas rice pudding with cream and almonds
excerpt: Rice is cooked low and slow in milk until thick, then chilled and folded with whipped cream and chopped almonds. Ris a l'amande is the centrepiece of the Danish Christmas dessert. A whole almond is hidden inside -- whoever finds it wins a prize.
sourceNotes: Ris a l'amande is the centrepiece of the Danish Christmas dessert. A whole almond is hidden in the bowl -- whoever finds it wins a prize. The name is French-influenced, dating from when French cuisine was fashionable among Scandinavian elites.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the rice pudding a day ahead and fold in the cream just before serving.

content.text: The rice pudding base must be completely cold before you fold in the cream. Warm rice will deflate the whipped cream and give you a loose, runny pudding rather than a light, airy one. Make it the day before and chill overnight.

items.prepNote: use 50g blanched almonds instead -- finely chopped and folded in at the end

content.text: Put rice and milk in a large saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often.
Reduce heat to very low. Cook for 35-40 minutes, stirring regularly, until the rice is very soft and the mixture is thick.
Remove from heat. Stir in caster sugar and vanilla. Spread onto a tray or pour into a bowl to cool faster. Once at room temperature, cover and refrigerate until cold.
Whip the double cream to soft peaks. Fold gently into the cold rice pudding. Fold in the chopped blanched almonds.
Hide one whole almond somewhere in the serving bowl. Serve cold with warm cherry or raspberry sauce.

items.cause: Milk reduced too much during cooking
items.fix: Stir in an extra 100ml warm milk while still hot to loosen -- it thickens further on cooling.

content.text: Denmark. A Christmas tradition taken very seriously. The almond-finding game is competitive -- the prize is traditionally a marzipan pig. The rice pudding is served cold, the sauce warm, and the contrast is intentional.
